subject: maths

subject: maths
name: Matching numerals to quantities

mastery_criteria: Chooses the numeral that tells how many are in a picture
Chooses the picture that shows a given number

subject: maths
name: Counting backwards from 20

subject: maths
name: One more and one less

subject: maths
name: Repeating patterns

mastery_criteria: Adds fractions with related denominators
Subtracts fractions with related denominators
Solves a word problem such as recipe amounts

subject: maths
name: Fractions as division
description: Sees a fraction as a division, such as 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4, and writes remainders as fractions or decimals.
mastery_criteria: Writes a division as a fraction
Shares 3 pizzas among 4 and names each share
Writes a remainder as a fraction

subject: maths
name: Fractions of a quantity
description: Finds non-unit fractions of quantities, such as 3/4 of 20, and works back to the whole from a part.
mastery_criteria: Finds 2/3 of 24
Finds the whole when 3/5 is 12
Solves a word problem with a fraction of an amount

subject: maths
name: Percentages of a quantity
description: Finds 10%, 25% and 50% and other familiar percentages of amounts by linking them to fractions and decimals.
mastery_criteria: Finds 10% of an amount by dividing by 10
Finds 25% as a quarter and 50% as a half
Finds 30% from 10%

subject: maths
name: Percentage discounts
description: Estimates and calculates discounts and sale prices for discounts such as 10%, 25% and 50%.
mastery_criteria: Calculates the discount on an item
Finds the sale price after a discount
Estimates a discounted price

subject: maths
name: Problems with decimals and money
description: Solves multistep problems with decimals, fractions and percentages in money contexts and checks with estimation.
mastery_criteria: Solves a multistep money problem
Checks the answer by estimating
Explains the steps and choices made

subject: maths
name: Converting metric units
description: Converts between kilometres, metres, centimetres, millimetres, kilograms, grams, tonnes, litres and millilitres using decimals, and compares measures in different units.
mastery_criteria: Converts 2.5 km to 2500 m and 750 g to 0.75 kg
Compares measurements by converting to the same unit
Reads a scale and records it as a decimal

subject: maths
name: Rectangle area problems
description: Uses length × width to find areas or missing sides, and compares rectangles with the same area or perimeter.
mastery_criteria: Finds a missing side from the area
Finds rectangles with a given area or perimeter
Compares the areas of rectangles with the same perimeter

subject: maths
name: Area of composite shapes
description: Finds the area of L-shapes and other shapes made from rectangles by splitting them or subtracting.
mastery_criteria: Splits an L-shape into rectangles to find its area
Finds an area by subtracting a cut-out rectangle

subject: maths
name: Area of parallelograms and triangles
description: Finds the area of a parallelogram by rearranging it into a rectangle, and of a triangle as half of a parallelogram.
mastery_criteria: Finds the area of a parallelogram from base and height
Finds the area of a triangle as half of base × height

subject: maths
name: Hectares and square kilometres
description: Uses hectares and square kilometres for large areas and knows 1 hectare = 10 000 m².
mastery_criteria: Knows 1 ha = 10 000 m²
Chooses m², ha or km² for an area
Finds the area of a large rectangle in hectares

subject: maths
name: Volume of rectangular prisms
description: Finds the volume of rectangular prisms in cm³ and m³ from layers or length × width × height, and uses water displacement for irregular objects.
mastery_criteria: Finds the volume of a rectangular prism
Finds two prisms with the same volume but different dimensions
Finds an object's volume from the rise in water level

subject: maths
name: Timetables and elapsed time
description: Reads timetables in 12- and 24-hour time and calculates the elapsed time between start and finish times.
mastery_criteria: Reads a bus or train timetable
Calculates elapsed time across the hour
Solves problems mixing 12- and 24-hour time

subject: maths
name: Angles on a line and at a point
description: Uses angles on a straight line (180°), angles at a point (360°) and vertically opposite angles to find unknown angles.
mastery_criteria: Finds an unknown angle on a straight line
Finds an unknown angle at a point
Uses vertically opposite angles

subject: maths
name: Four-quadrant coordinates
description: Plots and reads points with negative coordinates and describes how coordinates change when a point is moved or reflected.
mastery_criteria: Plots and reads points in all four quadrants
Says the new coordinates after a translation or reflection in an axis

subject: maths
name: Prisms, pyramids and cross-sections
description: Names prisms and pyramids by the shape of their base, compares their properties, and recognises the cross-sections of right prisms.
mastery_criteria: Names a prism or pyramid from its base
Compares the faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids
Picks the cross-section of a prism

subject: maths
name: Tessellations
description: Recognises shapes that tessellate and the combinations of transformations used to make tessellations and patterns.
mastery_criteria: Says whether a shape will tessellate
Names the transformations used in a tessellation

subject: maths
name: Range and mode
description: Finds the range and mode of a data set and compares the shapes of two distributions.
mastery_criteria: Finds the range of a data set
Compares two data sets using mode and range

subject: maths
name: Side-by-side graphs and timelines
description: Reads side-by-side column graphs for two categories and interprets timelines using their scale.
mastery_criteria: Compares two groups on a side-by-side column graph
Reads dates and intervals from a timeline

subject: maths
name: Misleading data in the media
description: Spots misleading graphs and possible bias in data shown in the media, and critiques the conclusions drawn.
mastery_criteria: Explains why a graph with a broken or uneven scale misleads
Identifies possible bias in how data was collected
Says whether a conclusion is supported by the data

subject: maths
name: Probability from 0 to 1
description: Gives probabilities as fractions, decimals or percentages on a scale from 0 to 1, and knows the probabilities of all outcomes add to 1.
mastery_criteria: Writes the probability of an outcome as a fraction
Places events on a 0 to 1 or 0% to 100% scale
Designs a spinner to match given probabilities

subject: maths
name: Expected and observed results
description: Compares expected and observed frequencies and explains why results get closer to the expected ones with more trials.
mastery_criteria: Finds the expected number of an outcome in a set number of trials
Compares observed results with expected results
Explains the effect of more trials and whether a game is fair

subject: english
name: Letter names and words in print
description: Names upper- and lower-case letters and tells letters apart from words, numerals and punctuation marks in print, signs and screens.
mastery_criteria: Names a letter shown in upper or lower case
Matches an upper-case letter to its lower-case partner
Picks out the word, the letter or the numeral in a short line of print
root_reason: Recognising letters and words in print is where school reading starts, so no earlier English topic is needed.

subject: english
name: Rhyming words
description: Hears whether two spoken words rhyme and picks or says a word that rhymes with a spoken word.
mastery_criteria: Says whether two spoken words rhyme (cat, hat)
Picks the rhyming word from three spoken words
Completes a familiar spoken rhyme with a rhyming word
root_reason: Rhyme is a listening skill children bring to school from songs and nursery rhymes, so nothing earlier in the syllabus is needed.

subject: english
name: Words in a spoken sentence
description: Listens to a spoken sentence of 3 to 5 words and says how many words it has and which word comes first or last.
mastery_criteria: Counts the words in a spoken sentence of 3 to 5 words
Says the first or last word of a spoken sentence
root_reason: Hearing separate words in speech is the first step of phonological awareness and builds only on everyday talk.

subject: english
name: Clapping syllables
description: Blends spoken syllables into a word and breaks spoken words of up to 3 syllables into syllables.
mastery_criteria: Counts the syllables in a spoken word of 1 to 3 syllables
Says the word when hearing its syllables (ba-na-na)
Splits a spoken word into syllables before spelling it

subject: english
name: First sound in a word
description: Says the first sound in a spoken one-syllable word and finds spoken words that start with the same sound.
mastery_criteria: Says the first sound of a spoken word (sun starts with /s/)
Picks the spoken word that starts with the same sound as a given word
Gives a word that starts with a given sound

subject: english
name: Blending sounds into words
description: Blends a spoken onset and rime (m–an) and then 3 or 4 separate spoken sounds (s–t–o–p) into a word.
mastery_criteria: Says the word after hearing an onset and rime (c–at)
Says the word after hearing 3 separate sounds (d–o–g)
Says the word after hearing 4 separate sounds

subject: english
name: Segmenting and counting sounds
description: Breaks a spoken one-syllable word into its separate sounds, counts them and names the first, middle and last sound.
mastery_criteria: Says each sound in a spoken CVC word (m–a–p)
Counts the sounds in a spoken word of up to 4 sounds
Says the middle or last sound of a spoken word

subject: english
name: Changing a sound to make a new word
description: Adds, takes away or swaps the first, last or middle sound in a spoken one-syllable word to make a new word.
mastery_criteria: Says the new word when the first sound changes (cat to hat)
Says the new word when the last sound changes (cup to cut)
Says the new word when the middle vowel sound changes (pin to pan)

subject: english
name: Letter–sound matches
description: Says the most common sound for each single letter and picks the letter that stands for a spoken sound.
mastery_criteria: Says the sound for a letter shown
Picks the letter that makes a spoken sound
Picks the letter a spoken word starts with

subject: english
name: Reading CVC words
description: Blends letter sounds to read vowel–consonant and consonant–vowel–consonant words such as at, sun and dog.
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed CVC word that matches a spoken word
Picks the CVC word that matches a picture or meaning (pig, peg, pug)
Reads 10 CVC words aloud to a grown-up with at least 8 correct (parent-marked)

subject: english
name: Spelling CVC words
description: Breaks a spoken CVC word into sounds and writes a letter for each sound to spell it.
mastery_criteria: Types a dictated CVC word correctly
Picks the correct spelling of a CVC word from three choices
Fills in the missing vowel in a CVC word (c_t)

subject: english
name: Consonant digraphs sh, ch, th and ck
description: Reads and spells CVC words where two letters make one sound, such as ship, chop, thin and duck.
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed word that matches a spoken word with a digraph (shop, chop, stop)
Types a dictated word with sh, ch, th or ck
Reads 10 digraph words aloud to a grown-up (parent-marked)

subject: english
name: Consonant blends in CCVC and CVCC words
description: Reads and spells words with two consonants together at the start or end, such as frog, stop, milk and best.
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed word that matches a spoken word with a blend (frog, fog, from)
Types a dictated CCVC or CVCC word (crab, milk)
Reads 10 words with blends aloud to a grown-up (parent-marked)

subject: english
name: Spelling ff, ll, ss, zz, ck and ve
description: Spells short-vowel words ending in ff, ll, ss, zz or ck (cliff, bell, dress, buzz, duck), knows these letter pairs do not start a word, and that words end in ve, not v (have, give).
mastery_criteria: Types a dictated word ending in ff, ll, ss or ck
Picks the correct spelling (duck, duk, duc)
Picks the correct spelling of a word ending in ve (have, hav)

subject: english
name: Reading vowel digraphs and split digraphs
description: Reads words with common vowel digraphs (see, moon, rain, boat) and split digraphs (cake, bike, home).
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed word that matches a spoken word (rain, ran, run)
Picks the word that matches a meaning when it differs only by a split digraph (hop, hope)
Reads 10 vowel digraph words aloud to a grown-up (parent-marked)

subject: english
name: High-frequency, compound and homophone words
description: Reads and spells taught high-frequency words such as the, I, was and said, simple compound words such as into and today, and common homophones such as to and two.
mastery_criteria: Picks a spoken high-frequency word from three printed words
Types a dictated high-frequency or compound word (into, today)
Picks to, too or two to fit a spoken sentence

subject: english
name: Adding s, -ing and -ed
description: Adds s to nouns to show more than one (cats) and -ing or -ed to familiar verbs (jumping, jumped) when the base word does not change.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that means more than one (dogs)
Picks the word that shows something already happened (jumped)
Types a dictated word ending in s, -ing or -ed where the base word does not change

subject: english
name: Sorting words into groups
description: Puts everyday words into groups such as animals, food, colours and clothes, and finds the word that does not belong.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that does not belong (apple, pear, chair)
Names the group a set of words belongs to
Picks a word that fits a named group
root_reason: Sorting familiar words uses the spoken vocabulary children bring to Kindergarten, so nothing earlier is needed.

subject: english
name: Words with two meanings
description: Knows that some words have more than one meaning (bat, bark, ring) and uses the sentence to pick the right meaning.
mastery_criteria: Picks the meaning of a word as used in a sentence
Picks the picture or meaning that matches a word in a sentence
Picks the sentence that uses a word with a different meaning

subject: english
name: Words and phrases for place and time
description: Understands words and phrases for size, position and time, such as big, under, behind, before, in the box and after lunch.
mastery_criteria: Picks the phrase that tells where (The ball is under the bed)
Picks the phrase that tells when (We eat breakfast in the morning)
Picks the size word that is the opposite of a given word (big, small)
root_reason: These everyday words and phrases for size, place and time come from talk at home and play, before any school English.

subject: english
name: What makes a sentence
description: Knows that a sentence makes sense on its own, with a subject (who or what) and a verb (what happens), and that changing the word order can change the meaning.
mastery_criteria: Picks the group of words that is a full sentence
Puts 3 or 4 jumbled words in order to make a sentence
Picks the subject or the verb in a simple sentence

subject: english
name: Capital letters, full stops and names
description: Starts a sentence with a capital letter and ends it with a full stop, and uses capital letters for names of people, places and days (proper nouns).
mastery_criteria: Picks the sentence with the capital letter and full stop in the right places
Picks the word in a sentence that needs a capital letter because it is a name
Shows where the full stop goes in a short sentence

subject: english
name: Question marks and exclamation marks
description: Ends a question with a question mark and a strong feeling or command with an exclamation mark, and a statement with a full stop.
mastery_criteria: Picks the right end mark for a question
Picks the right end mark for an exclamation
Picks the sentence that is a question

subject: english
name: Naming words and doing words
description: Finds the naming word (noun) and the doing word (verb) in a simple sentence.
mastery_criteria: Picks the doing word in a sentence (The frog jumps)
Picks the naming word for a person, animal or thing
Sorts words into naming words and doing words

subject: english
name: Adjectives
description: Finds and chooses describing words (adjectives) that tell more about a noun, such as big, red, soft and happy.
mastery_criteria: Picks the adjective in a sentence
Picks the adjective that best describes a noun
Picks which noun an adjective describes

subject: english
name: Pronouns
description: Uses pronouns such as I, he, she, it, we and they in place of a noun, and picks the right pronoun for a person or thing.
mastery_criteria: Picks the pronoun that can replace a noun (Mia: she)
Finds the pronoun in a sentence
Picks the right pronoun to complete a sentence

subject: english
name: Joining ideas with and, but and so
description: Joins two simple sentences with and, but or so, knows each part makes sense on its own, and says what the joining word adds.
mastery_criteria: Picks the joining word that best links two ideas
Picks the two simple sentences inside a compound sentence
Picks what so or but tells the reader

subject: english
name: Who, what and where
description: Listens to or reads 1 to 3 sentences and answers who, what and where questions using words from the text.
mastery_criteria: Answers a who question about a short text
Answers a what or where question about a short text
Picks the word or picture that matches a detail in the text
root_reason: Answering questions about a short text read aloud uses the listening comprehension children bring to school; decoding is not needed because the text is read aloud.

subject: english
name: First, next and last
description: Recalls the order of events in a short text and uses the words first, next, then and last.
mastery_criteria: Says what happened first in a short text
Says what happened last
Puts 3 events from a short text in order

subject: english
name: Characters, events and endings
description: Names the characters in a short story, tells what happened, and says how the story begins and ends.
mastery_criteria: Names a character in a short story
Says how a short story ends
Picks why a character acted the way they did

subject: english
name: Stories, information and persuasive texts
description: Tells whether a short text tells a story, gives facts or tries to get the reader to do or think something, and says what each kind of text is for.
mastery_criteria: Picks whether a short text entertains, informs or persuades
Says what a text is for (to entertain, to tell facts, to persuade)
Names a familiar kind of text such as a sign, a storybook or an advertisement
root_reason: Telling a storybook from a fact book draws on children's experience of books before school, so nothing earlier is needed.

subject: english
name: Segmenting words with blends
description: Breaks spoken words with three-consonant blends or blends at both ends (strap, crisp, splash) into every separate sound.
mastery_criteria: Counts the sounds in a spoken word with blends at both ends (c–r–i–s–p has 5)
Says the third sound of a spoken word that starts with a three-letter blend
Picks the spoken word that has 5 sounds

subject: english
name: Sound changes in words with blends
description: Adds, deletes or swaps a sound inside a consonant blend in a spoken word to make a new word (slip to sip, top to stop, frog to flog).
mastery_criteria: Says what is left when a sound in a blend is deleted (slip without l is sip)
Says the new word when a sound is added to make a blend (top to stop)
Says the new word when one sound in a blend is swapped (frog to flog)

subject: english
name: Digraphs ng, nk and wh
description: Reads and spells words with the digraphs ng, nk and wh, such as ring, think, when and wheel.
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed word that matches a spoken word (sing, sink, sit)
Types a dictated word ending in ng or nk
Picks the correct spelling (when, wen, whn)

subject: english
name: Longer blends: CCVCC and CCCVC words
description: Reads and spells one-syllable words with blends at both ends or three-letter blends, such as crisp, stamp, strap and splash.
mastery_criteria: Picks the printed word that matches a spoken word (strap, scrap, stamp)
Types a dictated CCVCC or CCCVC word
Reads 10 longer blend words aloud to a grown-up (parent-marked)

subject: english
name: Spelling vowel teams ee, oo, ai, oa and ay
description: Spells words where two vowel letters work together for one sound, such as feet, moon, rain, boat and play, and reads them in new words.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word with the same vowel sound as a spoken word
Types a dictated word with ee, oo, ai, oa or ay
Picks the correctly spelt word (rain, rane, rian)

subject: english
name: Spelling split digraphs a_e, i_e, o_e and u_e
description: Spells words with a split digraph, such as cake, bike, home and cute, and knows the e changes the vowel sound.
mastery_criteria: Reads the pair hop and hope and picks the one that matches a spoken word
Types a dictated word with a split digraph
Adds an e to change a word (kit to kite)

subject: english
name: Vowels with r: ar, or, er, ir and ur
description: Reads and spells words where a vowel and r make one sound, such as car, fork, her, bird and turn.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word with the same vowel sound as a spoken word (car: park, pack, pork)
Types a dictated word with ar or or
Picks the right spelling of the er sound in a known word (bird, berd, burd)

subject: english
name: One letter, more than one sound
description: Knows that a letter can stand for more than one sound, such as c in cat and city, g in got and gem, and y in yes, my and happy.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word where c sounds like s
Picks the word where y sounds like the y in my
Says which sound a letter makes in a given word

subject: english
name: Reading two-syllable words
description: Splits a written two-syllable word into syllables, knows every syllable has a vowel sound, and blends the parts to read words such as rabbit, picnic and sunset.
mastery_criteria: Picks where a written word splits into syllables (pic|nic)
Picks the vowel in each syllable of a two-syllable word
Picks the printed two-syllable word that matches a spoken word

subject: english
name: More high-frequency words
description: Reads and spells a growing bank of high-frequency words such as they, have, come, some, were and there.
mastery_criteria: Picks a spoken high-frequency word from three printed words
Types a dictated high-frequency word
Picks the correctly spelt high-frequency word (they, thay, theey)

subject: english
name: Word families
description: Builds a family of words from one base word (play, plays, played, playing, player) and works out what each word means.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that belongs to the same family as a base word
Finds the base word inside a longer word (jumping: jump)
Picks the family word that fits a sentence

subject: english
name: Topic words
description: Knows words that belong to topics learnt at school, such as weather, plants, families and seasons, and picks the word that fits a topic.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that belongs to a topic (weather: rain)
Picks the word that does not belong to a topic
Matches a topic word to its meaning

subject: english
name: Adverbs: when, where and how
description: Finds words that tell when, where or how something happens, such as yesterday, outside and quickly.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that tells how (The snail moved slowly)
Picks the word that tells when or where
Picks the adverb that best completes a sentence

subject: english
name: Finding facts in a text
description: Reads or listens to a short text of 2 to 3 sentences and finds facts stated in it to answer who, what, when and where questions.
mastery_criteria: Answers a when question using words from the text
Picks the fact that the text states
Picks the detail that is not in the text

subject: english
name: Simple inferences
description: Works out something a short text does not say directly, such as how a character feels or why something happened, using clues in the words.
mastery_criteria: Picks how a character feels from what they do
Picks why something happened when the text does not say
Picks the clue word that helped

subject: english
name: Titles, headings and contents pages
description: Knows what a title, heading, page number and contents page are for, and uses them to find information.
mastery_criteria: Picks the part of a book that lists its chapters
Picks the heading under which a fact would be found
Picks the best title for a short text

subject: english
name: Plot, character and setting
description: Names the characters, the setting (where and when) and the main events (plot) of a short story.
mastery_criteria: Picks the setting of a short story
Picks the main character
Picks the event that happened in the middle of the story

subject: english
name: Rhyme and alliteration in poems
description: Finds rhyming words and repeated first sounds (alliteration) in a short poem or chant and picks a word that keeps the pattern going.
mastery_criteria: Picks the two rhyming words in a short poem
Picks the word that keeps the alliteration going (silly snakes s...)
Picks the word that finishes a rhyming line

subject: english
name: Clues to a text's purpose
description: Uses clues such as made-up characters, facts, headings and opinion words to say whether a text is written to entertain, inform or persuade, and names common kinds of text.
mastery_criteria: Picks the clue that shows a text is trying to persuade
Picks the clue that shows a text gives information
Picks the kind of text, such as a recount, a report or a story

subject: english
name: Sound swaps in longer words
description: Deletes, adds or swaps sounds in longer spoken words, including inside blends (frog to fog, stand to sand), and uses this to read and spell new words.
mastery_criteria: Says what is left when a sound inside a blend is deleted (stand without t is sand)
Says the new word when a sound in a two-syllable word is swapped
Picks the printed word made by changing one sound

subject: english
name: Different spellings for long vowels
description: Knows the common spellings of each long vowel sound, including trigraphs and quadgraphs (ai, ay, a_e, eigh; ee, ea, y; igh, ie, i_e; oa, ow, o_e; oo, ew, ue, u_e), and picks the right one for a word.
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct spelling of a long vowel word (train, trane, trayn)
Types a dictated word with igh or eigh
Sorts words by their long vowel sound

subject: english
name: Vowel sounds ow, oi, aw, air and ear
description: Reads and spells words with the vowel sounds in cow, out, coin, boy, saw, chair and near, choosing between spellings such as ow and ou or oi and oy.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word with the same vowel sound as a spoken word
Types a dictated word with air or ear
Picks the correct spelling (cloud, clowd, claud)

subject: english
name: Silent letters and ph
description: Reads and spells words with silent letters (knee, write, lamb, gnat) and the less common digraph ph (phone, graph).
mastery_criteria: Picks the silent letter in a word
Types a dictated word that starts with kn or wr
Picks the correct spelling (phone, fone, phon)

subject: english
name: Compound words
description: Reads and spells compound words made of two smaller words (sunflower, playground, footpath) and knows each part keeps its spelling.
mastery_criteria: Picks the two words that make a compound word
Joins two words to make a compound word
Types a dictated compound word

subject: english
name: Double letters in the middle of words
description: Reads and spells two-syllable words with a double consonant after a short vowel, such as rabbit, happy and kitten.
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct spelling (rabbit, rabit, rabbitt)
Types a dictated two-syllable word with a double consonant
Picks the word that needs a double letter

subject: english
name: Endings tch and dge
description: Spells words ending in tch or dge straight after a short vowel (catch, fetch, badge, bridge), and ch or ge after other sounds (lunch, huge).
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct spelling (catch, cach, catsh)
Types a dictated word ending in tch or dge
Picks the word that ends with ch, not tch

subject: english
name: Tricky high-frequency words
description: Reads and spells high-frequency words whose spelling is not fully predictable from their sounds, such as because, friend, people and could.
mastery_criteria: Types a dictated tricky high-frequency word
Picks the correctly spelt word (friend, frend, freind)
Picks the tricky part of a high-frequency word

subject: english
name: Plurals with s and es
description: Chooses s or es to make a noun plural, adding es after s, x, z, sh and ch (buses, foxes, dishes, lunches).
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct plural (boxes, boxs)
Types the plural of a dictated noun
Says why a plural needs es

subject: english
name: Drop the e or double the letter
description: Drops the final e before -ing or -ed (make, making) and doubles the last consonant after a short vowel (hop, hopping; big, bigger).
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct spelling (making, makeing)
Picks the correct spelling (hopping, hoping) for a given meaning
Types a dictated word that drops an e or doubles a letter

subject: english
name: Comparing with -er and -est
description: Adds -er and -est to adjectives to compare things (tall, taller, tallest) and uses the right form in a sentence.
mastery_criteria: Picks the right form to compare two things
Picks the right form to compare three or more things
Types a dictated word ending in -er or -est

subject: english
name: Suffixes -ful, -ly and -y

subject: english
name: Discussions: more than one side
description: Knows the stages of a discussion (issue, points for, points against, conclusion) and tells a one-sided argument from a text that presents several viewpoints.
mastery_criteria: Picks the stage a paragraph belongs to in a discussion
Picks whether a text argues one side or presents several
Picks the point that belongs on the other side of an issue

subject: english
name: Persuading different audiences
description: Chooses the persuasive devices and language that best suit an audience, such as a letter to a council compared with a poster for children, and explains the choice.
mastery_criteria: Picks the sentence that would best persuade a given audience
Picks the device that does not suit an audience
Picks how a text changes its language for a different audience

subject: english
name: When and where a text was written
description: Uses clues in a text, such as objects, jobs, language and attitudes, to tell when and where it was written and how that shapes its ideas.
mastery_criteria: Picks when a text was most likely written
Picks the clue that shows the time or place
Picks an idea in the text that reflects its time

subject: english
name: Point of view
description: Identifies whose point of view a story is told from and explains how it shapes what the reader knows and feels about events and characters.
mastery_criteria: Picks whose point of view a passage is told from
Picks what the reader cannot know from this point of view
Picks how the passage would change if told by another character

subject: english
name: Sound devices in poems
description: Finds alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia, rhyme and repetition in a poem or song and explains their effect.
mastery_criteria: Picks the sound device in a line
Picks the line with assonance
Picks the effect of a sound device

subject: english
name: How characters change
description: Explains how and why a character changes from the start to the end of a narrative, using evidence from the text.
mastery_criteria: Picks how a character changes
Picks the event that causes the change
Picks the evidence that shows the change

subject: english
name: Greek roots
description: Uses common Greek roots such as tele (far), graph (write), phon (sound), bio (life), micro (small) and ology (study of) to spell words and work out their meaning.
mastery_criteria: Picks the meaning of a Greek root
Picks the word that contains a given root
Types a dictated word built from Greek roots

subject: english
name: Latin roots
description: Uses common Latin roots such as port (carry), struct (build), rupt (break), aqua (water), dict (say) and spect (look) to spell words and work out their meaning.
mastery_criteria: Picks the meaning of a Latin root
Picks the word that does not share a root with the others
Types a dictated word built from a Latin root

subject: english
name: Working out words from their parts
description: Breaks an unfamiliar technical word into prefix, root and suffix (in-spect-ion, bio-logy) to work out its meaning in a text.
mastery_criteria: Picks the meaning of an unfamiliar word from its parts
Picks the correct split of a word into prefix, root and suffix
Picks the technical word that matches a definition

subject: english
name: Words with unusual spellings
description: Reads and spells words with less common letter–sound matches, such as ache, choir, island, rhythm, scissors and yacht.
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct spelling (rhythm, rythm, rhythum)
Types a dictated word with an unusual spelling
Picks the silent or unusual letters in a word

subject: english
name: Easily confused words
description: Chooses correctly between easily confused words, such as affect and effect, practice (noun) and practise (verb), licence and license, and stationary and stationery.
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that fits a sentence
Picks the sentence where practice or practise is used correctly
Types the right word after hearing it in a sentence

subject: english
name: Endings -able and -ible
description: Usually chooses -able when a whole base word comes before it (enjoyable, washable) and -ible when the part before is not a whole word (visible, horrible).
mastery_criteria: Picks the correct ending for a word
Types a dictated word ending in -able or -ible
Picks why a word ends in -able

subject: english
name: Hyperbole
description: Recognises hyperbole (I've told you a million times) as deliberate exaggeration and explains why an author uses it.
mastery_criteria: Picks the sentence that uses hyperbole
Picks what a hyperbole really means
Picks why an author used hyperbole

subject: english
name: Emotive and vivid words
description: Picks out emotive and vivid words, explains the feeling or picture they create, and chooses a stronger word for effect.
mastery_criteria: Picks the most emotive word in a sentence
Picks the feeling a word choice creates
Picks the more vivid word to replace a plain one

subject: english
name: Formal and informal language
description: Tells formal from informal language and chooses words and sentences that suit the audience, such as a letter to the principal compared with a message to a friend.
mastery_criteria: Picks the most formal version of a sentence
Picks the informal word in a formal text
Picks the language that suits a given audience

subject: english
name: Embedded clauses
description: Finds and uses a clause embedded inside another clause, such as 'The boy who won the race was tired', to add detail without starting a new sentence.
mastery_criteria: Picks the embedded clause in a sentence
Picks the sentence made by embedding one clause in another
Picks the main clause left when the embedded clause is removed

subject: english
name: Commas with clauses and in dialogue
description: Uses commas to separate a dependent clause from a main clause, to mark off extra information, between items in a list and in dialogue.
mastery_criteria: Picks the sentence with the commas in the right places
Picks where a comma goes after an opening dependent clause
Picks how a comma changes the meaning of a sentence

subject: english
name: Brackets, dashes and hyphens
description: Uses brackets and dashes to add extra information, brackets for an acronym after the full name, and hyphens in compound words such as well-known and twenty-one.
mastery_criteria: Picks the sentence that uses brackets correctly
Picks the word that needs a hyphen
Picks what the words inside dashes add to a sentence

subject: english
name: Elaborated verb tenses
description: Recognises and uses elaborated tenses such as had finished, will have arrived and has been raining, and chooses precise verbs for meaning.
mastery_criteria: Picks the verb group that shows an action finished before another past action
Picks the verb form that completes a sentence
Picks the more precise verb for a sentence

subject: english
name: Nominalisation
description: Turns a verb or adjective into a noun (decide to decision, kind to kindness) to state ideas more briefly and formally.
mastery_criteria: Picks the noun formed from a verb
Picks the sentence that uses nominalisation
Rewrites a clause as a noun group by choosing the right nominalisation

subject: english
name: Word chains for cohesion
description: Finds how a text stays connected through repeated words, word associations (ocean, waves, tide) and words that stand in for earlier ideas (this, it, the problem).
mastery_criteria: Picks the word that belongs to a word chain in a passage
Picks what a word such as this refers back to
Picks the word that would best keep a passage connected

subject: english
name: Recognising bias
description: Compares subjective and objective language to spot bias, such as one-sided facts, loaded words and missing points of view.
mastery_criteria: Picks the more biased of two reports
Picks the loaded word in a sentence
Picks the point of view a text leaves out

subject: english
name: Comparing information from sources
description: Reads two short texts on the same topic, finds where they agree and disagree, and decides which is more reliable or detailed.
mastery_criteria: Picks a point on which two sources disagree
Picks the more reliable source and the reason
Picks a conclusion supported by both sources

subject: english
name: Glossaries, headings and diagrams
description: Uses a table of contents, glossary, headings, subheadings, tables and labelled diagrams to find and check information.
mastery_criteria: Picks where in a text to look for a word's meaning
Reads a fact from a simple table or labelled diagram
Picks the subheading under which a fact belongs

subject: english
name: Mixed-purpose texts
description: Explains how a text can combine purposes, such as a story that also informs or a report that also persuades, and how its structure and language work together to influence readers.
mastery_criteria: Picks the two purposes of a passage
Picks the part of a text that has a different purpose
Picks how the structure of a text helps persuade its readers

subject: english
name: Author's style
description: Identifies features of an author's style, such as sentence length, word choice, humour, dialogue and imagery, and picks the passage that matches a given style.
mastery_criteria: Picks the feature that marks an author's style
Picks the passage written in the same style
Picks the effect of an author's sentence lengths

subject: english
name: Imagery and sound in poetry
description: Explains how a poet uses imagery and sound together, such as metaphor with alliteration, to create meaning and effect.
mastery_criteria: Picks the image a line creates
Picks the sound device that supports the mood of a poem
Picks the line that best shows a poem's meaning

subject: english
name: Themes across texts
description: Identifies the theme of two short texts on a similar topic and explains how their messages are alike or different.
mastery_criteria: Picks the theme of each text
Picks how the two texts' messages differ
Picks the theme both texts share

subject: english
name: Symbols in literature
description: Explains what an object, colour or image stands for in a story or poem (a key for freedom, a storm for trouble).
mastery_criteria: Picks what a symbol stands for
Picks the object that is used as a symbol
Picks the evidence for a symbol's meaning
